sticker_location: Inside the tank, stamped on the back wall above the water line.

problems.title: Keeps running
symptoms: It runs on and off by itself
I hear water trickling in the toilet

plan.diagnosis: Water is leaking past the flapper, the rubber seal at the bottom of the tank, so the tank keeps refilling. Usually the chain catches or grime stops the flapper sealing, and a wipe and a chain fix stops it.
replacement_parts: Universal 2-inch toilet flapper (only if yours is warped)

steps.instruction: Lift the tank lid off
details: It's heavy porcelain; set it on a towel on the floor.
steps.check: The lid is off and resting on a towel.

steps.instruction: Check the chain has a little slack
details: Too tight holds the flapper open; too long gets caught under it.
steps.check: The chain hangs with about half an inch of slack.

steps.instruction: Turn the water off and flush
details: The valve is on the wall behind the toilet; turn it right.
steps.check: The tank is empty.

steps.instruction: Wipe the flapper and its seat
details: Use a rough sponge on the ring.
A warped or stiff flapper should be replaced; they're universal.
steps.check: The flapper and the ring under it feel smooth.

steps.instruction: Turn the water back on
details: Turn it left all the way.
steps.check: The tank fills and then goes quiet.

steps.instruction: Flush once and listen
details: Silence after a minute means it's fixed.
steps.check: It fills and then stops completely.

problems.title: Still running with a good flapper
symptoms: Still running with a good flapper

plan.diagnosis: With a good flapper, the water level is probably set too high, so it trickles into the overflow tube and never stops. Lowering the float a little stops it.

steps.instruction: Lift the tank lid off
steps.check: The lid is off.

steps.instruction: Look where the water ends
details: The water should stop about an inch below the top of the tube.
steps.check: You can see water spilling into the open tube.

steps.instruction: Lower the float a little
details: Turn the long screw on top of the fill valve, or squeeze the clip and slide the float down an inch.
steps.check: The float sits lower on the valve.

steps.instruction: Flush and check the level
steps.check: The water stops an inch below the top of the tube.

problems.title: Weak flush
symptoms: The toilet doesn't flush all the way

plan.diagnosis: A weak flush usually means the flapper isn't lifting all the way, because the chain is too long, or the tank isn't filling all the way because the water valve is partly closed.

steps.instruction: Lift the tank lid off
steps.check: The lid is off.

steps.instruction: Hold the handle down and watch the flapper
details: It should lift straight up and stay up for a few seconds.
steps.check: You can see how far the flapper lifts.

steps.instruction: Shorten the chain to half an inch of slack
details: Move the clip one or two links.
steps.check: The chain has just a little slack.

steps.instruction: Open the wall valve all the way
details: Turn it left until it stops.
steps.check: The valve is fully open.

steps.instruction: Flush and watch
steps.check: Everything goes down in one flush.

problems.title: Clogged or overflowing
symptoms: The water is rising in the bowl

plan.diagnosis: Something is stuck in the bowl's trap. Stopping the water first keeps it from overflowing, then a few firm plunges usually clears it.
safety: Never mix drain cleaners in a toilet; the fumes are dangerous.
If sewage comes up in a tub or floor drain too, call a plumber.

steps.instruction: Don't flush again: lift the tank lid
details: If the bowl is rising, act fast.
steps.check: The lid is off.

steps.instruction: Push the flapper shut to stop the water
details: Press it down with your hand; it's clean tank water.
steps.check: No more water goes into the bowl.

steps.instruction: Turn off the water at the wall
details: Turn it right until it stops.
steps.check: The tank stops filling.

steps.instruction: Plunge with slow, firm pushes
details: Use a plunger with a flap (flange) that fits the hole.
Seal it, push gently first, then pump firmly 10 times.
steps.check: The water drains away with a gulp.

steps.instruction: Turn the water back on and flush
steps.check: It flushes and refills normally.

problems.title: Fills slowly or not at all
symptoms: No water goes into the tank

plan.diagnosis: Grit from the water line clogs the top of the fill valve. Turning the water off, popping the cap and flushing the grit out usually fixes it.

steps.instruction: Lift the tank lid off
steps.check: The lid is off.

steps.instruction: Turn the water off at the wall
details: Turn it right.
steps.check: The valve is closed.

steps.instruction: Twist off the fill valve cap
details: Push down and turn it left an eighth of a turn.
steps.check: The cap is off.

steps.instruction: Hold a cup over the valve, water on for 5 seconds
details: This flushes grit out of the line.
steps.check: Clear water sprays into the cup, washing the grit out.

steps.instruction: Put the cap back and turn the water on
steps.check: The tank fills in about a minute.
